head: claude/alpaca-trade-scoped-close-20260908
title: Trade-scope the Alpaca close OPERATION and modify_protective (Tier-3, landing: hold — the venue CAN express it)
body:
## ⚠️ `landing: "hold"` — `tier_2_3_needs_approval`. Tier-3 order path.

Implements `WO-20260908-TRADE-SCOPE-THE-ALPACA-CLOSE-OPERATION-AND` from MI-173's measurement in #11312.

Opened **ready, not draft** — per the 2026-09-03 operator ruling, the hold lives in `.github/pr-landing/`, which is machine-readable and enforced, never in the draft flag. **Nothing here merges on its own**: no automerge request file is written, and R4 bars `landing: self` for any Tier-3 diff whatever its approval state.

---

## 0. The first step was a QUESTION, and it came back YES

MI-173 explicitly could not establish whether Alpaca supports a quantity-scoped close, and listed it as the proposal's first step. **It does.**

`DELETE /v2/positions/{symbol_or_asset_id}` documents a `qty` query parameter — *"the number of shares to liquidate. Can accept up to 9 decimal points. Cannot work with percentage"* — read from the Alpaca API reference on 2026-09-08.

So the "venue cannot express it" branch of the done-condition does **not** apply and the operator's approval holds. Had the answer been no, the finding would have been the deliverable and nothing here would have been patched.

## 1. What was wrong

The per-trade quantity travelled the whole chain and was dropped at the venue boundary:

```
order_monitor._send_close_to_exchange   qty = matched_trade["position_size"]   <- 16, or 56
  -> execute.close_open_position(qty=...)  validates `if qty <= 0` ...
        if exchange == "alpaca":  exchange_client.close(symbol)   <- ... then NEVER PASSES IT
  -> AlpacaClient.close(self, symbol)    <- the signature has no qty parameter at all
```

Closing the 16-share row on a symbol the account was short 72 of liquidated all 72; the sibling row stayed `open` with nothing behind it.

## 2. The change, and why its blast radius is bounded

Scope is resolved from **one live position read, taken before anything destructive** (`_resolve_close_scope`). Three outcomes:

| condition | path | change vs `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `qty` omitted, or `qty` >= live position | whole-symbol flatten | **byte-for-byte unchanged** — pre-cancel, cancel-settle, `qty_available` gating, strict flat-confirm |
| `qty` < live position | `?qty=N` reduction, **cancels nothing** | new path |
| position unreadable | **defer** (`retCode 2`) | new — never falls back to a flatten |

The first row is every single-row symbol, i.e. almost every close. The new behaviour applies **only** where other shares on the symbol genuinely belong to somebody else.

**The pre-cancel is a second destructive step, and the partial path does not reach it.** `_cancel_open_orders_for_symbol` cancels *every* resting order on the symbol, so a close of A strips B's stop and target **before** the flatten is attempted — leaving B naked on any path where the flatten then fails. On the partial path we issue the reduction against whatever is available and, if the venue refuses for want of free shares, **report that** (naming what holds them, via the existing `classify_share_hold`) rather than cancelling our way through. A loud failure is correct; the alternative is a silent over-close.

**"We did not look" never becomes "liquidate everything."** An unreadable position defers.

**Extended hours defers a partial exit rather than attempting one**, and says why: that path cannot be made trade-safe without either cancelling the sibling's bracket or stacking a duplicate close-limit every tick (a resting extended-hours limit of ours is indistinguishable from a protective take-profit on the side we are closing). The bracket stays armed; the exit costs one session — the same posture the `closed` branch already takes. Reversible, and named as a deliberate narrowing rather than left as a gap.

**`modify_protective` gets the same scoping and refuses rather than guesses.** No matching leg -> `retCode 1`, naming the quantities that do rest. Two same-side legs of the same size -> `retCode 1`, naming the ambiguity. Refusing leaves the existing stop where it is (conservative); the alternative moves a stop that belongs to another trade.

**The mislabelled success log is fixed.** It read `qty=16 -> alpaca flatten` while the venue liquidated 72 — a per-trade number printed next to an operation that ignored it, on the only per-close record a reviewer would find. Sub-class A. The label now comes from the client's own answer: `WHOLE-SYMBOL flatten — the venue closed the entire TLT position, not just this trade's 16`, or `TRADE-SCOPED close of 16 share(s)`, with the request shown as `requested_qty=` and never as what happened.

## 3. The confirmation — read this part in two halves

Constraint: **do not extend #11279's confirmation change to Alpaca.** I did not. But a trade-scoped operation forces a confirmation question, so here is exactly what was decided and by whom.

**(a) The partial-fill rule is `strict`, and that is not a new choice.** A reduction that lands only partly (10 of a requested 16) does **not** confirm — `retCode 1`, row stays open, monitor retries. That is the answer the operator already gave for IB on 2026-09-08, recorded in `OPEN-PRS.json`: *"erring toward a phantom OPEN row that existing reconcilers clean up, rather than a phantom CLOSED row that fabricates PnL on the remainder and leaves lots naked."* Same answer, mirror venue, not a default that drifted.

**(b) The MEASUREMENT is what is genuinely open for Alpaca.** #11279's approval scope says so in terms: *"EXPLICITLY NOT Alpaca — Alpaca's mirror defect is decided separately on #11312."* Here the **whole-symbol path keeps its strict "the symbol must disappear" gate untouched**, and only the **new** partial path measures the trade's own quantity delta — because a partial close can never satisfy a flatness gate, and would otherwise report failure forever while retrying, eating the sibling's position a slice at a time.

**Why this does not reinstate `BL-20260707`'s false-SUCCESS:** that hazard is confirming a 16-share reduction against a venue that liquidated 72. It requires the confirmation to be loosened *ahead of* the operation. Here the measurement is loosened only for a path whose operation was narrowed **in the same commit**, and the pre-existing path's gate is untouched. **That ordering is the safety property and it is the thing to check.** If you disagree with the ordering argument, this is the line to push on.

## 4. Test plan — the population, stated honestly

- [x] **14 new tests**, run against `main`'s `src/` verbatim (stashed): **12 failed, 2 passed.** Three groups, and the middle one is easy to miscount as evidence:
  - **TEN fail on behaviour** — these are the repair.
  - **TWO fail only with `TypeError: AlpacaClient.close() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`** — they pass a quantity that has no parameter on `main`. That is the absence of the feature, not a behavioural difference. They pin that the whole-symbol path *did not change*, so **by construction they cannot demonstrate a change**, and they are not counted as evidence.
  - **TWO pass on both trees** — the only true either-way controls, and the only two that establish the legacy no-qty path is untouched.
  - The split is restated in the test module's own docstring so it survives this PR body.
- [x] **Two pre-existing tests updated because they pinned the defect**: `test_close_open_position_routes_alpaca` asserted `close.assert_called_once_with("SPY")` (the dropped qty) and `test_modify_open_order_routes_alpaca` asserted the un-scoped `modify_protective` call. Both now pin the fixed contract, with the reason in-line.
- [x] **Full suite: 15529 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed** (16m00s, clean tree).
  ⚠️ **An earlier run of the same suite reported 1 failure and it was MINE, not the diff's** — recorded because a green number that replaced a red one should say why. `test_guards_uncommitted_work.py::test_only_a_guard_that_actually_runs_stays_quiet` observed a dirty tree because I ran `run_guards.py` concurrently and `training-population-guard` writes `docs/training-population-matrix.md` mid-run. Diagnosed (it passes in isolation), then **re-run cleanly with nothing concurrent** rather than argued away — the number above is that re-run.
- [x] **Guards:** `run_guards.py --base main` -> **PASS 68 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 22**. (`layer-guard` first failed with `exited 127`; `lint-imports` was simply not installed in this sandbox. Installed it and re-ran — `Contracts: 6 kept, 0 broken`.) `check_pr_landing.py --base origin/main` -> `OK — state=declared_needs_approval`. `check_wip_ceiling.py` -> 4 in flight against a ceiling of 8.
- [ ] CI green — see the arming note below.

**NOT established, stated rather than filled in:**
- **Live acceptance of `?qty=` against a real Alpaca position.** No broker call was made from this session. That remains an `alpaca_paper` verification step. What is established is the documented parameter and this repo's use of it.
- **Whether any over-close has ever actually fired.** That was MI-171's measurement; I did not reproduce it.
- How often two simultaneously-open Alpaca rows on one symbol carry the *same* size — the case `modify_protective` now refuses. MI-173 found one Alpaca pair (16 and 56, different sizes, so the heuristic resolves it). I did not extend that count. **We did not look.**

## 5. Hard constraints — what I deliberately did NOT do

- **MI-140 is untouched.** No change to account capability gating, `config/accounts.yaml`, or `side_filter`. `alpaca_live`'s immunity (it cannot place orders) is exactly as it was. Nothing here remediates it.
- **#11279's confirmation change is not extended to Alpaca** — see section 3.
- **`partial_close` is NOT added to the Alpaca caps.** That capability gates `_send_partial_close_to_exchange`, the exit-ladder's scheduled scale-out — a different feature with its own journal accounting. I only corrected the stale *comment* that justified its absence with a claim the venue disproves (*"the flatten endpoint closes the whole position"*). Field beats comment; the capability stays unwired.
- **No live positions were touched.** MI-179 is concurrently re-arming the 56 naked TLT shares; this unit is code only.

## Filed for follow-ups

Two rows, both found while doing this and both left unfixed on purpose, filed through `backlog_append.py::append_row` (searched first; 28 insertions / 0 deletions, no reformat):

- **`BL-20260908-ALPACA-PROTECTION-IS-NOT-TRADE-ATTRIBUTABLE-AT-ALL`** — filed with `similar_ok` as a deliberate sibling of `BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY` (lexical overlap 0.88, and **not** a duplicate: that row's criterion 2 was met **for IB only**, via `oca-protect-t<trade_id>`; Alpaca got neither half). `trades.sl_order_id`/`tp_order_id` are written on exactly one path, gated to Bybit partial-tpsl, so they are NULL for every Alpaca trade by construction — and `place_protective` sets no `client_order_id` either. **That is why `modify_protective` must match on quantity**, and why it refuses on equal-sized siblings. The refusal is correct given the missing handle, but it is a capability gap standing in for a fix.
- **`BL-20260908-ALPACA-CANCEL-ORDERS-ESCALATION-USES-AN-UNDOCUMENTED-PARAM-ON-THE-PER-SYMBOL-ENDPOINT`** — the close path's *"strongest programmatic lever left"* sends `?cancel_orders=true` to `DELETE /v2/positions/{symbol}`, where Alpaca documents no such parameter. It is documented **only** on `DELETE /v2/positions` (close-ALL). Both pages read 2026-09-08, so the contrast is measured. Either Alpaca ignores the unknown parameter — making the escalation a no-op identical to the retry that just failed, and its "escalation also failed" log a misattribution — or it honours it undocumented. **I could not distinguish them and made no broker call.** `OI-20260901`'s GLD wedge, where that lever "also failed", is consistent with a no-op but does not prove one.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — no schema, model-boundary, pipeline-stage, deployment, public-API or config-shape change. `AlpacaClient.close` / `modify_protective` gain an optional keyword; every existing caller and both retCode envelopes are backward-compatible.

---

### Housekeeping

- ⚠️ **I could not post the mandatory board START claim.** #6927 is at GitHub's hard 2500-comment cap — writes 403. Known and parked (MI-182); **not retried**.
- ⚠️ **`create_pull_request` 403'd for this session**, so this PR is opened through `automation/pr-requests/` and `pr-opener.yml`. That means it is opened by `github-actions[bot]`, and **GitHub fires no workflows for `GITHUB_TOKEN` actions** — so a `total_count` of 0 or 1 on the checks API means CI never ran, not that it passed. One ordinary commit follows to arm it.
- The work object is moved `dormant` -> `in_flight` with one **assessed** `blocked_on` edge (the Alpaca confirmation *measurement*), plus an `evidence` block carrying the capability answer and the test population. ⚠️ The MI-140 coupling is deliberately **not** written as an edge: MI-140 is held until *this* lands, so the dependency runs the other way, and recording it backwards would make the constraint computation read a deadlock that does not exist.
- ⚠️ **`landing: hold` means this needs a merge click.** It is not waiting on an approval to be *re-sought* — the operation change is approved. It is waiting on a human, and on the section-3(b) measurement question.
